events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $3.00 (model confidence 0.66)
events.body:
This is a RydeTAXI trip (Hougang Mall → Changi T3) charged $42.25 metered, so the metered structure applies and any unexcused extra distance enters the fare [F7][RD-2]. The trace settles that an off-route segment exists: F3 shows segment 21:58–22:05 driven 4.04 km where the optimal route covers 1.90 km, adding 2.13 km, up to 1209 m off the optimal route [F3][RD-1]. The trace also settles there is no qualifying incident on the replaced stretch (F15; a speed band alone does not exempt) [F15][RD-4].

The only exemption candidate is consent. The chat is complete and every message is timestamped [F10]. Before the segment began at 21:58, the driver asked at 21:55 whether he could "go round via Tampines Avenue 7" and the rider replied at 21:56 "可以，走 Tampines Avenue 7 吧" — a rider message, sent before the segment, expressly naming that road [F8][F9][RD-5]. This is a SPECIFIC named-road authorisation, so it covers driving on Tampines Avenue 7 only, and the record must tie the driven segment to that road. Nothing in the fact table names the roads of the driven path: no message places the car on Tampines Avenue 7 after 21:56, and the only post-trip statement is the driver's own claim that he turned off via that road, which is a claim, not consent, and does not independently supply the path tie [F9][F11]. Because the record cannot settle whether the driven segment is the agreed road, that element is undetermined rather than exempt [RD-5].

Reading the consent in context, however, the rider did not merely authorise a route to the destination: the agreement was given to a route that the driver said was needed because of congestion, i.e. an ordinary route choice to reach Changi T3, not an errand or excursion of the driver's own; there is no stop, no loop reaching nothing, and no place chosen by the driver at all in the record [F8][F9][F3]. The deviation is therefore explained as an agreed congestion-avoidance route, and the excess does not represent a detour the driver forced on an unwilling rider — but the absence of any record tying the segment to the specifically named road leaves it open, and RydeTAXI metered fare means the extra kilometres were actually billed [F4][F7][RD-2].

The trace states this finding changes the amount, so an undetermined segment cannot be silently resolved. Because the amount at stake is small ($3.00) and the record cannot settle the path tie, the just result is the middle course: not full exemption, not a finding of a forced detour. The billed excess attributable to the unexcused extra distance is $3.64 (2.58 km × $1.4098/km, this trip's distance fare ÷ distance km), of which the segment's own extra km is 2.13 km [F4][F3][RD-2]. $28.28 ÷ 20.06 km = $1.4098/km; 2.13 km × $1.4098/km = $3.0029 → $3.00 [F7][F4][RD-2]. The waiting amount $0.11 is a metered waiting unit, not refundable under RD-3(c) [F5][RD-3]. No account flag: F18 shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0, so RD-6 does not apply [F18][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read both chat messages, the driver's statement and the complaint. They contain a route negotiation and the rider's query about the fare ("我不确定他走的是不是他说的那条路") — no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation [F8][F9][F11]. No safety concern arises [SAFE-1].

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: We reviewed your Changi T3 trip. You were charged for extra distance driven off the route, and $3.00 of that is being refunded to you as a Ryde voucher. A short stretch off the fastest route was taken, and while route changes were discussed in chat, the record doesn't show the road you discussed was the road actually driven, so part of the fare wasn't justified. The rest of the metered fare, including waiting time, stands. No action is needed from you — the voucher will be added to your account. Thanks for flagging it.

DRIVER: We reviewed the route on the Hougang Mall to Changi T3 trip. A stretch of the drive left the fastest route, and the record doesn't tie that stretch to the road the rider agreed to, so $3.00 of the distance fare is being returned to the rider as a Ryde voucher. The route change discussed in chat was a normal congestion-avoidance choice, not an excursion, so this is logged as a minor route issue on your record. No account flag or suspension applies. Keep to the agreed road, or confirm any change with the rider, so it's clear on the record.

Reading the consent in context, however, the rider did not merely authorise a route to the destination: the agreement was given to a route that the driver said was needed because of congestion, i.e. an ordinary route choice to reach Changi T3, not an errand or excursion of the driver's own; there is no stop, no loop reaching nothing, and no place chosen by the driver at all in the record [F8][F9][F3]. The deviation is therefore explained as an agreed congestion-avoidance route, and the excess does not represent a detour the driver forced on an unwilling rider — but the absence of any record tying the segment to the specifically named road leaves it open, and RydeTAXI metered fare means the extra kilometres were actually billed [F4][F7][RD-2].

The trace states this finding changes the amount, so an undetermined segment cannot be silently resolved. Because the amount at stake is small ($3.00) and the record cannot settle the path tie, the just result is the middle course: not full exemption, not a finding of a forced detour. The billed excess attributable to the unexcused extra distance is $3.64 (2.58 km × $1.4098/km, this trip's distance fare ÷ distance km), of which the segment's own extra km is 2.13 km [F4][F3][RD-2]. $28.28 ÷ 20.06 km = $1.4098/km; 2.13 km × $1.4098/km = $3.0029 → $3.00 [F7][F4][RD-2]. The waiting amount $0.11 is a metered waiting unit, not refundable under RD-3(c) [F5][RD-3]. No account flag: F18 shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0, so RD-6 does not apply [F18][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read both chat messages, the driver's statement and the complaint. They contain a route negotiation and the rider's query about the fare ("我不确定他走的是不是他说的那条路") — no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation [F8][F9][F11]. No safety concern arises [SAFE-1].

Since the segment's extra distance of 2.13 km was billed in a metered fare, it stands as a refundable unexcused segment under the middle course where the path tie cannot be established [F3][F4][RD-2]. Three kinds of agreement: (1) GENERAL route choice ('take whichever way is faster') covers a route chosen to get there, not an errand of the driver's own (a stop away from the route, a loop that reaches nothing: counts). (2) A SPECIFIC named road or area ('go round via X') covers driving on X only: the record must tie this segment to X (a stop on X, a message placing the car on X, a road name in a fact); timing alone does not, and the fact table carries no road names for the driven path — if nothing ties them, the finding is undetermined (G13); if the record places this segment somewhere else (a stop away from X, the driver's own statement naming another road or place, a stop the driver chose the location of), the agreement to X does not cover it: counts.
